Catalog override lifetime. A whitelist read rejects while an injected capturing catalog coroutine is pending. The join unwinds the dependency object; the pending coroutine can resume through its destroyed closure. Hold the catalog callable in rt::async before starting its Promise.

Refresh override lifetime. A refresh child rejects while a sibling created by an injected capturing refresh coroutine is suspended. Handler exit destroys the callback holding its captures; the sibling can still resume. Wrap each injected callback in rt::async with copied options.

Provider selection override lifetime. The selection read rejects while an injected capturing catalog coroutine is pending. Handler exit destroys the callable; the pending build can resume through it. Hold the catalog callable in rt::async before starting its Promise.

SSE completion keeps a body-outcome latch alive through its logging reaction. If transport header preparation throws before reading, runtime can finish a fallback response without ever cancelling the SSE body. The body latch retains the log, process permit and request drain indefinitely. Cancel the unconsumed body when native response setup fails.

src/handler/terminal_route.cpp.note: Reviewed admission, quota gates, terminal accounting hooks, routes and background exception replay.

sites.detail: The outer route or scheduled omission owns state, request and identifiers. Permit callbacks own state and are transferred through responses, while borrowed admission helpers are awaited directly.
The outer route retains the receiver, and terminal settlement callbacks copy its shared state into logging. Both reservation tasks keep their receivers through waits.

Every route factory owns shared State in its direct awaiting frame and each downstream task gets an owning context or a borrow from that retained State. No sibling can outlive the frame through a fail-fast join here.

An injected Task-returning persistence callable can be stored in the Promise-returning std::function through implicit Task adoption. A successful background registrar lets the options frame die while that coroutine is pending. Invoke a shared copy of the callable and keep that same copy in the persistence settlement chain.
The owning route frame holds State, authentication, permit and quota context. Task factories pass values into children or run only while an owner in the awaiting chain remains live.

src/health.cpp.note: Reviewed passive fan-out, provider bindings and the active-probe timeout race.

sites.detail: Auth hash children take a whole account or string copy, and independent health and quota operations own their arguments. Cache and endpoint bodies are named frame values.
Active probe tasks own account or credential, optional KV, signal and shared progress. Aggregation reads copies or uses shared progress on the same loop after child completion.

The probe or its failure can win, then finalization clears the only timer that settles the private timeout Promise. That pending source retains the combined outcome and the active result until the process loop ends. Use withResolvers and settle the timeout loser after clearing its timer.
Coalescing copies the in-flight promise before waiting. Passive joins use independent tasks and subsequent views point into the named tuple or immutable frame snapshots.

src/http.cpp.note: Reviewed synchronous OpenAI error/JSON creation, CORS and request-response helpers. Headers and other input views are consumed synchronously and outputs retain the required response/body handles.

src/images.cpp.note: Reviewed request-body and multipart parsing, image fan-out and cancellation coordination, response aggregation and public adapters.

sites.detail: File tasks and form parsing retain their byte and request owners. The file loop traverses a private unchanged vector, and the body cleanup guard's references remain in its own frame.

Fan-out callbacks and child tasks each own their shared state. The child waits with its context and dispatch closure live, allSettled waits for every child, and response reordering uses fresh local iterators.
The facade copies context before making the Task, and the frame owns parsed variants, response vectors and upstream receiver handles. No other child mutates the vectors during traversal.

src/inference_admission.cpp.note: Reviewed release callbacks, fair queue updates and queued abort/timer ownership.

sites.detail: All queue and map mutations execute synchronously. Permit release owns the controller and normal grant, caller abort and timeout remove the waiter and its event listener before resolving.

A queued waiter owns its listener and the listener strongly captures both that waiter and its controller. Dropping an isolated loop before the unreferenced wait timer fires drops the timer without invoking abort, so the controller, entries and signal remain in a cycle. Let registered waits use weak listener captures and put the lease of controller ownership in an external clearable timer.

src/inference_deadline.cpp.note: Reviewed the three stream/paid timer factories and request-deadline signal composition.

sites.detail: Timer callbacks copy the abort controller and active flag, and returned handles use timer identity. The timer owns no callback that retains its returned deadline handle, and clear or expiry releases the registration.

src/input_normalization.cpp.note: Reviewed synchronous payload, tool, message and schema normalizers. Any reference-capturing algorithms run inline and normalization owns its output. No suspension or deferred callbacks.

src/responses_stream.cpp.note: Reviewed stream framing, abort and timeout races, generator delegation, proxy lifecycle callback ownership, preflight and SSE heartbeats.

sites.detail: The abort listener owns only reader control and weakly references the signal. Disposal removes it, while detached cancel has already acquired a stream owner.

Orphaned Responses inactivity race. The upstream read wins and the code unregisters the only inactivity rejection callback. The pending inactivity source owns its race reaction and the winning ReadResult, retaining a chunk for every ordinary read. Settle that private loser after removing the listener and only after its race has been installed.
Frames points into the consuming coroutine's own unchanged chunk while yielding. The generator captures are retained by the generator runtime and its delegated task owns the session.
The iterator and callback dispatchers put copied state, reason or event into Task frames before asynchronous use. Proxy pull also holds state after controller.close clears callbacks.

The newPromise executor uses this only synchronously and its timer uses weak state. Cancellation and read wins resolve the synthetic heartbeat even when stopping the timer. A heartbeat win leaves the same read pending until a chunk or cancel.
Preflight and stream factories transfer values to generator and source holders. Escaping cancellation and pull tasks take copied iterator, stream control or source state before the wrapper returns.
